articles.title: Crushed review – Steve Oram is priestly lead in harrowing Bangkok-set child-abduction thriller
articles.summary: A priest investigates his daughter’s kidnapping in Thailand in this Paul Schrader-esque inquiry into spiritual nihilism. ‘He’s American, a little bit overweight, sweaty, a little bit camp, creepy.” As far as descriptions of border-hopping paedophiles go, this seems a little on the nose.
body: Pastor to a mixed Anglo-Thai congregation, Father Daniel has a young daughter, Olivia (Margaux Dietrich), with wife May (Nattapohn Rawddon). At a sleepover, Olivia is traumatised when her friend’s older brother shows her a “crush” video of a kitten being stomped by a scantily clad floozy. So when her own cat Missy goes awol, she is convinced the same lady is responsible, and asks her dad how God could let it happen. The family mobilise to track down Missy, but Olivia in turn disappears one day after school, kicking off Father Daniel’s own test of faith.

There could have been a very different version of Crushed, if Liam Neeson had signed on with his special set of ecumenical skills. But Rumley holds the vengeance angle at bay, subtly foreshadowing Olivia’s ordeal with the implied horror of the squashed furballs filtering through her nightmares, and using clever juxtaposition to slyly compare and contrast her father’s lofty ideals with the surrounding scrappy reality. At one point, after refusing to play the Beatles’ profane songs, Father Daniel’s acoustic guitar version of All Creatures Great and Small soundtracks Olivia’s pet search on the streets.

articles.title: ‘Should have garnered the actor an Oscar’: why Liar Liar is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our series of writers paying tribute to the films they watch when they need a lift is an appreciation of Jim Carrey’s manic 90s comedy. To be completely honest, whenever anybody asks what my favorite movies are, my list has some typical standbys: Goodfellas and It’s a Wonderful Life…
body: The movie (for the lack of a better word) lies on the bedrock of a simple premise: a lawyer and doting father is physically unable to tell an untruth due to a birthday wish. In the hands of a less competent creative team and cast, Liar Liar would have been yet another forgettable piece of 90s comedy junk; destined for the bottom of a discount VHS bin, forgotten as the years trudged on. But largely thanks to an unbelievable performance courtesy of Carrey, who was working with a smart and peppy script, the film thusly ascends into rarefied air.

The bellylaugh-o-meter breaks its springs on a regular basis throughout its brisk 86-minute runtime. In fact, it’s on par, or even surpassing, fellow comedy powerhouses such as Airplane! and The Naked Gun when it comes to the sheer volume of gags, setpieces and jokes. Tom Shadyac, the director, who previously directed Carrey in his 1993 breakout Ace Ventura: Pet Detective, wisely unleashes Carrey, who spins out and around the scenery like the Tasmanian Devil, remarkably combining such a manic and energetic performance with one grounded in pure emotion.

articles.title: International Oscar Submissions: Italy, France, Spain, Poland, Indonesia and More Join the List
articles.summary: The campaigns for the Oscar for international feature film are gaining momentum, with final submissions due by Oct. 1. The Oscars shortlists will be revealed on Dec. 15, with 15 international films selected to be voted on by Academy members in all branches who commit to watch all 15 films.
body: This year’s entries include titles like Romania’s “Fjord,” which won the Palme d’Or at Cannes; Chile’s “The Meltdown,” which screened in Un Certain Regard; Germany’s “Everytime,” which won Cannes’ Un Certain Regard prize; France’s “Minotaur,” which won the Cannes Grand Prix; Spain’s “La Bola Negra” and Poland’s “Fatherland.”

Meanwhile, a new Academy rule allows any film that wins the top prize at one of the six biggest festivals — Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Sundance, Busan and Toronto — to be entered in the international feature race even without a national committee’s backing.
Bangladesh has selected “Roid,” directed by Mejbaur Rahman Sumon, as its official submission for the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards.
The Bangladeshi drama had its premiere as a Tiger Competition selection at International Film Festival Rotterdam ‘s 55th edition. “Roid” was also selected for the Seattle International Film Festival.

articles.title: Just Play Dead review – Samuel L Jackson and Eva Green punch up switchback crime caper
articles.summary: Jackson and Green just about manage to distract viewers from the sub-par Tarantinoesque flourishes, confusing plot points and tired stereotypes. Having shot five films since 2020, 82-year-old Martin Campbell is a certified member of the post-retirement director’s club that includes Ridley Scott…
body: Interrupting his retirement on a Spanish-speaking Caribbean island with the odd poisoning (seen in the intro), kingpin Jack Wolfe (Jackson) is getting antsy. Afraid the law is close behind him, he hatches a scheme with his philandering wife Nora (Eva Green): help him frame her surfer lover Chad (Jason Fernández) for his supposed murder, and they will split the big-bucks insurance payout. He covers his back for the possibility she might do him in for real by recording her saying as much. But she ropes Chad anyway into her murder conspiracy, plotting to let him take the fall – or perhaps her detective bit on the side Dani (Eoin Macken) will get there first.

articles.title: Florence Pugh Speaks Out Over Cornell University Sexual Assault Case: ‘We Need Our Men to Be as Horrified and Sickened as Us’
articles.summary: Florence Pugh has posted a lengthy statement on social media in response to a controversy that has erupted at Cornell University over an alleged sexual assault incident that took place two years ago.
body: In a post on Instagram on Sunday, Pugh described described the incident as an “horrific act,” adding that she knew “this has happened before, and I hate the idea of it happening again.” She also urged men to speak out and to be “leading conversations about how we change the allowance and complicity of this behaviour as much as we are.” She concluded: “Be angry for us. Please.”

The statement from Pugh comes just days after she outlined her long-standing support for Palestine, telling Vanity Fair t hat she didn’t know “why it took so long for people to start talking and for people to actually feel sympathy.”

After reading about the young woman who was gang raped at her college by her friend and school peers, I’m feeling uneasy and sick and anxious. I’m processing quietly and watching everything and everyone and every man. I have a few thoughts on this horrific act that happened at Cornell College in 2024. I know this has happened before, and I hate the idea of it happening again.

articles.title: Kikuyu Land review – the colonial-era misery behind our morning cup of tea
articles.summary: The impact of colonial then corporate agricultural development is unravelled in a sobering documentary that takes a dramatic turn when a family secret is discovered. The central highlands of Kenya are renowned for their lush tea plantations, which stretch as far as the eye can see.
body: The film then takes a dramatic turn when Wangondu discovers an uncomfortable family secret: her beloved grandfather, a well-respected landowner, was also a perpetrator of colonial abuse. The shattering revelation not only collapses the distance between Wangondu and her subjects, but also points to other forms of complicity. For lovers of tea worldwide, Kikuyu Land suggests that ordinary consumers take a cold hard look at where their product comes from.

articles.title: China Box Office: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Tops Pre-Holiday Weekend
articles.summary: Marvel Studios’ “Avengers: Endgame Encore” claimed the top spot at the mainland China box office during the Sept. 25–27 frame, grossing RMB83.8 million ($12.5 million) over the weekend, according to Artisan Gateway. The Marvel epic’s cumulative lifetime haul in China is now $647.8 million.
body: Riverrun Grace Film’s crime comedy “The Old Fox” debuted in fourth place, pulling in $3.6 million. Directed by Li Taige, the film stars Yu Qian as a retiring veteran police officer who discovers suspicious anomalies during an apparently routine theft investigation. When his inquiry leads directly to a ruthless corporate chairman played by Tony Leung Ka-fai, the two seasoned operators become locked in a battle of wits.

Rounding out the top five, Pearl River Film Group’s crime thriller “V” took $2.8 million in its sixth frame to lift its cumulative gross to $96 million. Directed by Han Yan (“Love Never Ends”) and featuring an ensemble cast led by Tony Leung Ka-fai, Zhu Yilong, Tan Jianci, and Kara Wai, the film chronicles an ambitious man’s rapid ascent to power and the lingering consequences that threaten his success.

Mainland China’s overall weekend grosses reached $39.9 million amid a customary quiet corridor ahead of the impending Golden Week holiday. The 2026 year-to-date box office stands at $4.34 billion, down 29.4% compared to the same period in 2025.

articles.title: Angela Scanlon takes over Sara Cox's drivetime slot on Radio 2
articles.summary: The station also announces a new presenter for its country show after Bob Harris's departure.
body: Angela Scanlon is to take over BBC Radio 2's drivetime show after Sara Cox moved to the breakfast slot.
The Irish personality said it was "properly exciting" to be hosting the station's 16:00-19:00 show every weekday from November.
She said: "Millions of people, all having completely different days, piling into the same conversation for a few hours - what a strange and lovely thing!"

Scanlon, who hosted a Sunday early morning programme on the station from 2018 to 2021, was among a number of people who filled in after Cox vacated the drivetime slot in May, including Joel Dommett, Jason Manford, Ellie Taylor, Alex Jones and Gary Davies.

articles.title: Taylor Swift breaks record for most MTV VMAs as Madonna also wins
articles.summary: Swift took home the big award for video of the year on a night when the original Queen of Pop performed.
body: Taylor Swift took home the video of the year award as she became the most successful artist in the history of the MTV Video Music Awards on Sunday.

The singer went into the night tied with Beyoncé on 30 wins, and went on to score the night's top award for the visuals for her track The Fate of Ophelia, taken from her 2025 album The Life of a Showgirl.

The original Queen of Pop, Madonna, won artist of the year, best dance and best collaboration alongside Sabrina Carpenter for their dancefloor-filler Bring Your Love, which was the lead single from Madonna's 2026 album Confessions II.
Swift also received the inaugural award for artist director, having written and directed the glitzy and theatrical Ophelia music video herself.
points: Swift took home the big award for video of the year on a night when the original Queen of Pop performed.

articles.title: You Must Watch This Korean Netflix Reality Show That Makes The Traitors Look Like Kids' Stuff
articles.summary: If you like The Traitors, get a load of this Korean reality show on Netflix that makes Alan Cumming's show seem like child's play.
body: Everyone is rightfully obsessed with "The Traitors," Peacock's gloriously trashy reality show about contestants backstabbing and outwitting each other across a sprawling Scottish castle that isn't actually owned by host Alan Cumming. But what if I told you that show, for all its lowbrow pleasures, is continuously outclassed by a production from South Korea?

"The Devil's Plan" traps a group of contestants on a lavish soundstage set. They live together, eat together, hang out together, and regularly engage in cutthroat competitions to increase a pile of cold, hard cash as they're eliminated one-by-one. But here's the kicker: Everyone in the game was cast for their intelligence, and the games they play are built to break even the smartest member of the cast. A combination of celebrities, doctors, lawyers, professional gamers, science experts, and even board game enthusiasts clash over brain-burning challenges that push them to the mental limits, often shattering social contracts in the process.
points: If you like The Traitors, get a load of this Korean reality show on Netflix that makes Alan Cumming's show seem like child's play.
